headline: Ghana's Late Knife Through Panama's Wall
story: Ghana suffocated Panama in Toronto with a masterclass in compact defending, ceding 56 per cent possession while forcing 49 turnovers and pressing in five distinct phases. Panama controlled the tempo but found their host immovable: Lawrence Ati-Zigi's steadiness under fire and Jonas Adjetey's positioning meant the 11 shots yielded only four on target. Ghana, meanwhile, absorbed pressure with a 22.4-second ball recovery—nearly double Panama's tempo—and waited. The script flipped entirely in the 90th minute.

When Ghana's moment came at 90+5, it carried an expected value of 0.97—a clinical finish that Panama's 0.77 xG could not match. Two Panama chances emerged too late: at 90+9, consecutive efforts of 0.24 xG each were saved, the finishing rushed and the goalkeeper alert. Caleb Yirenkyi's 7.9 rating drove Ghana's intensity; Amir Murillo's 7.2 for Panama could not override a fundamental imbalance—one side organised, one overstretched. Extra time punished possession without purpose.

keyMoment.text: Ghana's goal: the only shot that mattered, arriving when Panama's resistance cracked.

home.verdict: Smothered Panama's passing game and struck when it counted—but nearly paid for inviting 56% possession.
points: High-press discipline (5.4 phases) forced turnovers; maintain this shape against teams that dominate the ball.
22.4-second recovery time is your fortress; any quicker and you risk being overrun by rapid transitions.
0.97 xG on one shot: clinical efficiency. Protect that—don't trade control for late chances against sharper opponents.

away.verdict: Possession without penetration; controlled the game but left Yirenkyi and Adjetey unpunished.
points: 11 shots, 4 on target: 36% accuracy is wasteful. Improve conversion or Panama's possession phases become liability.
0.77 xG versus Ghana's 0.98 tells the story; tighter finishing on those two 90+9 chances would have changed everything.
12.2-second ball recovery beat Ghana's 22.4 but you never capitalised; faster transitions mean nothing without a killer finish.

statLine: Ghana's single shot on target found the net in the 90th minute; Panama's four shots and 56 per cent possession found only draws in a tournament that punishes profligacy.
